Question B-003-015-004.

Why the correct answer is right: A packet network links packet-radio stations so data can be forwarded beyond a single direct path.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "A way of connecting packet-radio stations so data can be sent over long distances": This is the correct choice because a packet network links packet-radio stations so data can be forwarded beyond a single direct path.
- sourceIndex 1: "A way of connecting terminal-node controllers by telephone so data can be sent over long distances": This is a near-miss because it shifts attention from A way of connecting packet-radio stations so data can be sent over long distances. In digital information, packet forwarding, weak-signal modes, and sound-card drive level, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
- sourceIndex 2: "The connections on terminal-node controllers": This answer would fit a different fault than A way of connecting packet-radio stations so data can be sent over long distances. In digital information, packet forwarding, weak-signal modes, and sound-card drive level, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
- sourceIndex 3: "The programming in a terminal-node controller that rejects other callers if a station is already connected": This option confuses another station topic with A way of connecting packet-radio stations so data can be sent over long distances. In digital information, packet forwarding, weak-signal modes, and sound-card drive level, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
